destination.name: Lithgow
destination.tagline: A coal and steel town west of the Blue Mountains, with a steam railway, glow-worm tunnel and sandstone pagodas close by.
destination.description: Lithgow is a city of 11,197 people (2021 urban area) about 150 km west of Sydney, the first true country town west of the Blue Mountains and a former coal-mining and iron-and-steel centre. The Lithgow Zig Zag railway was built between 1866 and 1869 to climb the mountains, was superseded in 1910 and now runs as a heritage steam railway. Around town are national parks: Wollemi National Park holds the 387 m Glow Worm Tunnel, and Gardens of Stone National Park has rock pagodas and canyons in a World Heritage area. The Capertee Valley, described as one of the widest enclosed canyons, lies to the north.
whyVisit: See rock pagodas at Gardens of Stone
Walk to the Glow Worm Tunnel

goodToKnow.title: Glow Worm Tunnel road
goodToKnow.detail: The tunnel is reached by a graded dirt road of about 30 km from Lithgow; 2WD can manage it but 4WD is recommended, and bring a torch for the dark centre section.

goodToKnow.title: Check closures
goodToKnow.detail: A park fire ban at Glow Worm Tunnel runs until 31 March 2027, and Gardens of Stone may close for poor weather or fire danger.

goodToKnow.title: Book the Zig Zag
goodToKnow.detail: Zig Zag Railway runs four daily rides of 45 minutes to 1 hour 45 minutes and recommends booking online.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are best for the walks, since NPWS advises visiting Glow Worm Tunnel on weekdays or in spring or autumn to avoid the crowds and limited parking of summer.
